Computation of default maximum blocks and inodes and parsing and formatting of huge mode tokens are absent.
Mempolicy acquisition display and release behavior and quota load enable and dquot helper internals are absent.
Inode creation, offset context, extended attribute, ACL and file attribute helper internals are absent.
Remainder of per size huge store after mode lookup, including non PMD policy handling, is truncated and absent.

findings.text: Remount entry validates proposed limits and flags against live superblock state and, when checks pass, commits huge mode, inum width, block and inode caps, derived free space, mempolicy reference and noswap flag.

A remount that proposes block or inode caps is rejected when the live instance is currently unlimited, and is also rejected when current block usage or derived inode space usage already exceeds the proposal.

Width reduction to narrow identifiers is rejected once the next identifier exceeds the narrow range, enabling of swap prohibition is one way, quota activation on remount is rejected when no quota is loaded, and any change to configured global quota hard limits is rejected.

Reconfiguration holds the superblock statistics raw spinlock across usage sampling, all limit and flag checks, and the commit of limits and flags, releasing it on both success and failure, with the replaced mempolicy reference dropped only after release.

Options display reports size, inode count, mode, owner and group only when they differ from defaults, then conditionally reports identifier width, huge setting, NUMA policy, swap prohibition and active quota types with configured hard limits.

Identifier width display is always shown when wide identifiers are active or when wide identifiers are the build default, and is hidden only when narrow identifiers are active while narrow is also the build default.

Superblock creation allocates zeroed info rounded against false sharing, installs defaults and caller identity, initializes locks lists counters and UUID, wires operations and quota state, and creates the root directory.

Ordinary mounts inherit system default block and inode caps and default identifier width when the corresponding option was not seen, and record the requested swap prohibition, while kernel internal mounts are marked as not for user space.

Superblock info carries maximum block and inode counts, derived free inode space, owner, group, mode, wide identifier flag, huge preference, mempolicy pointer, swap prohibition flag, quota limits, statistics lock, shrink list with its lock, and per CPU identifier batch for kernel mounts.

Superblock teardown releases encoding resources, disables quotas, frees per CPU batch, destroys block usage counter, drops mempolicy reference, cleans extended attribute cache where present, frees info and clears the filesystem private pointer.

Context operations bind context release and nodev tree construction, with monolithic parsing, single parameter parsing and reconfiguration available for the configurable build, and the filesystem type registers under tmpfs with user namespace, identifier mapping and managed time behavior.

Context initialization allocates zeroed mount options, sets world writable sticky directory mode and caller filesystem user and group identities, clears encoding state where applicable, attaches context operations and requests inode versioning.

Monolithic mount string splitting ends an option at a comma only when the following character is not a decimal digit, so commas inside numeric node lists remain part of the same option, and iteration ends with a null cursor.

User and group inode hard limit options are parsed as sizes, rejected on trailing characters or zero value and on exceeding a quota ceiling before storing into option limits, case folding options delegate to a dedicated helper, and strict encoding without unicode support is rejected.

Operation tables assign address space handling with no-op dirtying and optional write and migration paths, file handling for mapping open seek IO sync splice allocation and leases, inode handling for attributes links directories symlinks and ACLs, superblock handling for inode lifecycle statistics display quota eviction and huge reclaim, and virtual memory handling for faults page mapping NUMA policy and userfaultfd.

Early initialization creates the inode cache, registers quota format and filesystem, creates the kernel internal mount, initializes feature sysfs, and applies the global huge preference to the internal mount with a default that inherits PMD order when per order state was not configured.

Superblock creation failure funnels through teardown to avoid leaking allocated info and initialized objects, and early initialization failure unregisters filesystem and quota format, destroys the inode cache, and records the error in the internal mount pointer.

Global huge control shows all supported modes in fixed order with the active mode bracketed, and its store path accepts a short newline terminated token, parses it into a huge level, updates the global and internal mount preference when above the deny threshold, and restarts the background collapse service.

Mutual exclusion for per order huge preferences uses a dedicated spinlock held while moving one order bit into the selected mode set and clearing it from all other mode sets, reporting whether any set changed.

Per size preference exposes five modes with at most one owning a given order, display brackets the first owning mode in table order and otherwise brackets never, and stores resolve the requested token to a mode index before exclusively reassigning that order.

Filesystem identity uses tmpfs as registered name with TMPFS_MAGIC as superblock magic, page sized blocks, maximum regular file size as size ceiling, unit time granularity and donotcache root behavior.

Feature sysfs uses write only, read write and read only attribute helpers with conventional permission encodings, groups optional case folding support under a features group attached to a tmpfs object, and reports case folding availability with a fixed supported marker.
Global huge store rejects input that does not fit a small stack buffer with terminator, copies only the supplied length, guarantees termination and strips a single trailing newline before parsing.
Case insensitive lookup support is provided by directory entry operations that delegate hashing and comparison to generic folding helpers.
Folio error removal is defined as an always successful no operation.

Inode objects come from a dedicated cache with once initialization, allocation may fail with null, release frees any symbolic link target before returning the object, destruction releases shared NUMA policy for regular files and offset state for directories, and the cache itself is created with panic and accounting semantics and destroyed at teardown.
